test_title: PYST 22: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - GA (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements about the squash court measurements and markings:
1) Short line: 4.26 m from back wall in singles, 4.57 m in doubles.
2) Tin: 48 cm high strip at front wall, like tennis net.
3) The half-court line and the short line essentially forms a L with the back wall as base.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2 are Correct**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Statement 1: Short Line Measurements**: 
 
 
• In a **singles squash court**, the short line is marked at a distance of **4.26 m from the back wall.** 
 
• In a **doubles squash court**, the short line is positioned at **4.57 m from the back wall.** 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
 

 
• **Statement 2: Tin Height**: 
 
 
• The **tin** is a **48 cm high strip** located at the front wall of a squash court. 
 
• Its purpose is similar to that of a tennis net, acting as a lower boundary for valid shots. 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
 

 
• **Statement 3: Half-Court Line and Short Line Forming an L**: 
 
 
• The **half-court line** and the **short line** intersect at the center of the court to divide it into four quadrants. 
 
• However, this does not form an "L" with the back wall as a base; instead, it forms a “T” shape at the center. 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**.
 
 

 
• *Based on the above analysis, only statements 1 and 2 are correct.*
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Squash Court Dimensions:** 
 
 
• The **singles squash court** measures 9.75 m (length) by 6.4 m (width). 
 
• The **doubles squash court** is larger, measuring 13.72 m (length) by 7.62 m (width). 
 
• The height of the court walls varies but must meet international standards set by the World Squash Federation (WSF). 
 
 

 
• **Purpose of the Tin:** 
 
 
• The tin prevents players from hitting the ball too low on the front wall. Any ball that strikes the tin is considered out. 
 
• In professional squash, it adds a level of precision and difficulty for players.
 
 

 
• **Markings on the Squash Court:** 
 
 
• The **short line** divides the court into front and back halves. 
 
• The **half-court line** divides the back half into two equal parts, creating left and right service boxes. 
 
• The **service boxes** are used to initiate play during serves. 
 
 

 
• **Rules of Squash:** 
 
 
• The objective is to strike the ball onto the front wall within the boundaries, ensuring it doesn’t hit the tin or go out of bounds. 
 
• The ball must bounce only once on the floor before being returned by the opponent.
 
• Matches are typically played in a best-of-5 games format, with each game requiring a player to score 11 points to win. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **World Squash Federation (WSF):** 
 
 
• WSF is the international governing body for squash, responsible for setting court dimensions, rules, and tournament guidelines. 
 
• It ensures uniformity across professional tournaments and oversees the development of the sport globally.
 
 

 
• **Squash Ball Specifications:** 
 
 
• Squash balls are made of rubber and vary in bounce levels, indicated by colored dots (e.g., double yellow for professionals). 
 
• The choice of ball depends on the players’ skill level and court temperature.
 
 

 
• **Safety in Squash:** 
 
 
• Eye protection is mandatory in many tournaments to prevent injuries from the fast-moving ball. 
 
• Proper footwear with non-marking soles is recommended to ensure grip and prevent damage to the court surface. 
 
 
 
57:T23
